layers.note: A canopy tree of wet ground near salt water and along streams; local in the south Puget Sound lowlands.

moisture.note: Wet ground: stream banks, swamp edges and seeps; tolerates saturated soil.

heat_load.note: Prefers cool, humid sites; scarce on hot, dry slopes.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 600 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Mostly on flats and lower slopes.

shade_tolerance.note: Moderately shade tolerant: grows up under alder and in gaps.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −6 °C, gone by −12 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −24 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −32 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 11 to 22.5 °C; gone below 9 °C, where summers are too short, and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: Across its range, about 700 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 350.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.7, gone by 0.6.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Sitka spruce grows in the coastal fog belt from Kodiak Island to northern California, rarely more than 80 km inland; in Alaska it reaches the tree line (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
